title: Outil d'évaluation complet de l'abord intraveineux difficile (C-DIVA)
formula:
The C-DIVA score is derived by summing the selected points:

| Variable | Points | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Visual appearance | Many visible veins | 0 |
| Few visible veins | 1 | |
| No visible veins | 2 | |
| Palpable sites | Many palpable veins | 0 |
| Few palpable veins | 1 | |
| No palpable veins | 2 | |
| History of difficult access | No difficulty | 0 |
| Reported difficulty or recent missed attempts | 1 | |
| History of major difficulty as evidenced by previous central lines of PICC s | 2 | |
| Clinical factors | Not applicable | 0 |
| Pediatric patients; urgent conditions ( ESI 3-4) | 1 | |
| Comorbidities; emergency conditions (ESI 1-2) | 2 | |

how_to_use.why: Permet de reconnaître précocement le moment où il faut passer à des techniques alternatives pour obtenir un abord destiné à l’administration de médicaments et de fluides.
how_to_use.when: Utiliser pour identifier les patients à risque d’accès intraveineux (IV) difficile.
how_to_use.pearls:
- Aide les cliniciens à stratifier les patients selon un risque faible, moyen ou élevé d’accès IV difficile.
- Peut être utilisé dans de multiples contextes, y compris au service des urgences.
- En tant que score ponctuel, le score du patient peut varier dans le temps en fonction de l’évolution de son état clinique.
- La catégorie « Facteurs cliniques » peut être subjective, car elle énumère de manière générale les comorbidités (sans nommer de pathologies spécifiques) et les situations urgentes par opposition aux situations d’urgence nécessitant un accès intraveineux.
- Les premiers scores d’accès IV difficile séparaient les adultes des patients pédiatriques ; cet outil s’applique à tous les âges et intègre l’âge dans le score lui-même.

next_steps.advice:
- Cet outil ne doit pas être utilisé comme seul prédicteur d'un abord veineux périphérique difficile ; il convient de tenir compte du tableau clinique global et de faire preuve de jugement clinique pour chaque patient.
- Lors de l'utilisation de cet outil, tenir compte de la gravité de l'état du patient et de sa stabilité hémodynamique pour choisir la méthode d'abord la plus appropriée à l'administration des médicaments et à la réanimation.
next_steps.critical_actions:
Pour les **scores ≥6,** envisager d’autres options d’accès vasculaire, y compris, sans s’y limiter :

- Cathéter périphérique sous guidage échographique.
- Accès intra-osseux.
- Cathéter central à insertion périphérique.
- Cathéter veineux central.

evidence:
[van Loon et al.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27100437/)developed the A-DIVA scale in a prospective, observational, cross-sectional cohort study of 1,063 adults (≥18 years) scheduled for any surgical procedure, regardless of [ASA class](nabda:calc.asa-physical-status-asa-classification) , demographics, or medical history. Patients were excluded if they could not understand or respond to the questionnaire (due to physical or communication disorders), were unresponsive, or if peripheral IV access had already been obtained on the ward prior to study participation. The primary outcome was failure of first-attempt peripheral IV cannulation. The authors proposed a 5-variable, additive bedside scale based on readily observable features (including vein palpability and visibility, history of difficult IV access, urgency of surgery, and vein size), intended to identify patients at risk for difficult access and support earlier escalation to alternative techniques (e.g., ultrasound). Key limitations included single-center design and derivation in a perioperative population (which may limit generalizability to settings such as the ED).

[van Loon et al.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30691137/)subsequently performed a prospective, multicenter, multidisciplinary validation study across 5 hospitals in the Netherlands, enrolling 3,689 patients and analyzing 3,587 after exclusions (e.g., inability to provide informed consent, inability to understand the questionnaire, IV already obtained, and protocol violations/data issues). Adults >18 years were included regardless of indication for IV access, demographics, or medical history, and participants came from multiple specialties and units with staff trained in the protocol and routinely obtaining peripheral IVs. The primary endpoint, again, was a failed first-attempt at peripheral IV cannulation. The validated model used 5 predictors: history of difficult IV cannulation, difficult IV access as expected by the practitioner, inability to palpate a vein, inability to visualize a vein, and vein diameter <3 mm. Strengths included multicenter design, large sample size, and broadened inclusion beyond perioperative patients; limitations included geographic restriction and a focus limited to the first attempt rather than overall cannulation success.

[Bell et al.](https://www.gavinpublishers.com/article/view/validation-and-reliability-of-the-comprehensive-difficult-iv-access-scoring-tool)reported a prospective, observational validation and reliability study focused on inter-rater agreement for a comprehensive difficult IV access scoring tool. C-DIVA was developed after reviewing A-DIVA and was intended as a more broadly applicable, point-of-care scoring system to support earlier escalation decisions. The study surveyed 7 nurses with known vascular access experience; no exclusions were listed. Outcomes included validation of the score and assessment of inter-rater agreement, with authors concluding the tool could be used to support escalation decisions. Important limitations were the very small, non-random sample, scenario-based design without clinical outcomes, and modest inter-rater reliability (55.6% agreement; intraclass correlation coefficient 0.49).
more_info:
Interprétation :

| Score C-DIVA | Risque | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0-3 | Faible | Obtenir un accès IV |
| 4-5 | Moyen | Obtenir un accès avec un praticien compétent ; envisager une consultation VAS |
| 6-8 | Élevé | Envisager une intervention d'urgence (CVC, IO) ; consulter le VAS immédiatement |
